public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Heirloom Carbon is a Series B climate & energy company that has raised $150M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set spanning 1 public comparable (LNZA) and 8 private companies in the frontier climate-tech sector, including KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy, which collectively provide stage-relevant benchmarks.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $150M total raised as a proxy baseline, applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $285M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comps—KoBold Metals ($3.0B, Series C), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B, Series C), and Amogy ($700M, Series C)—produces a median of $1.0B, with a range of $700M to $3.0B. The stage-progression method is more conservative, reflecting the company's earlier funding stage relative to the peer set.

Triangulation of these two methods supports a valuation range of $242M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median estimate of $642M. Key uncertainties include the company's capital efficiency relative to peers, near-term revenue trajectory, and technology de-risking progress. The wide peer range ($700M–$3.0B) reflects meaningful dispersion in how frontier climate investors are currently valuing similar-stage businesses, suggesting that fundraising outcomes will depend significantly on investor conviction around unit economics and commercialization timeline.
